successCriteria.description: The `Employee` entity interface is defined in `src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts` with all required fields: id (string), employeeNumber (string), firstName (string), lastName (string), email (string), managerId (string | null), department (string), hireDate (Date), terminationDate (Date | null), employmentStatus (EmploymentStatus — imported from `src/shared/types`), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date).

The `IEmployeeRepository` interface is defined in `src/modules/employee/employee.repository.ts` with all required methods: `findById(id: string): Promise<Employee | null>`, `findByEmployeeNumber(employeeNumber: string): Promise<Employee | null>`, `findByManagerId(managerId: string): Promise<Employee[]>`, `findAll(): Promise<Employee[]>`, `create(employee: Omit<Employee, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>): Promise<Employee>`, `update(id: string, data: Partial<Employee>): Promise<Employee | null>`.

A stub `EmployeeRepository` class is provided that implements `IEmployeeRepository` and throws "not implemented" (or an equivalent descriptive error) from every method — no real database access in this phase.

Jest unit tests exist at `tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.model.test.ts` verifying that the `Employee` interface shape is structurally correct (all fields present with correct types, EmploymentStatus imported from shared types).

Jest unit tests exist at `tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts` verifying that the stub `EmployeeRepository` throws on every method call, and that the `IEmployeeRepository` interface contract is structurally correct.

constraints: The `Employee` entity interface must import `EmploymentStatus` from `src/shared/types/index.ts` — do not redefine or duplicate the enum locally.

The `IEmployeeRepository` interface must use `Omit<Employee, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>` as the input type for `create` — the repository (not the caller) is responsible for generating `id`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`.
The `update` method must accept `Partial<Employee>` and return `Promise<Employee | null>` — `null` signals the entity was not found; the caller decides whether that is an error.
No database access, no Knex imports, no SQL in this phase. The stub `EmployeeRepository` must be a pure TypeScript class with no external dependencies beyond the model interface.
outOfScope: Real database-backed `EmployeeRepository` implementation (Knex/PostgreSQL) — deferred to a later phase. This phase provides only the stub.
`IEmployeeService` / `EmployeeService` — the service interface and implementation are deferred to Phase 10 per PLAN.md.
Fastify routes, controllers, or HTTP handlers for the employee module — no API surface in this phase.
Database migrations (Knex) for the `employees` table — deferred to the phase that delivers the real repository implementation.

ambiguities.description: Should `Partial<Employee>` in the `update` method allow callers to pass `id`, `createdAt`, or `updatedAt`? The repository must ignore or reject attempts to overwrite `id` and `createdAt`, and should set `updatedAt` itself. The code agent should decide whether to use a stricter type (e.g., `Partial<Omit<Employee, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>>`) or document the behaviour.
options: Use Partial<Employee> as-is and document that id/createdAt are ignored
Use a stricter Omit type to prevent callers from passing those fields

entityInvariants.invariant: Every Employee must have a unique `employeeNumber` and a unique `email`. The repository interface exposes `findByEmployeeNumber` to enforce this lookup contract; the uniqueness constraint itself is enforced at the database layer in a later phase.

`managerId` is a self-referencing foreign key: it must be either `null` (top-level employee) or a valid `id` of another Employee. The repository does not enforce this in the stub phase, but the interface must accept `string | null` to support the manager hierarchy.
`employmentStatus` must be one of the `EmploymentStatus` enum values: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, or TERMINATED. The type system enforces this via the import from `src/shared/types`.

`terminationDate` must be `null` when `employmentStatus` is ACTIVE, and must be set when `employmentStatus` is TERMINATED. This invariant is documented in the entity interface (via comments or type narrowing) but enforced at the service layer in a later phase.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth rule at the repository layer — auth is enforced at the service/controller layer in later phases.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns `null` when no employee exists with the given id — does not throw.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth rule at the repository layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must return the created Employee with `id`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` populated. The stub throws "not implemented"; the real implementation will throw on unique constraint violations (duplicate employeeNumber or email).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth rule at the repository layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the updated Employee on success, `null` if no employee with the given id exists. The `data` parameter is `Partial<Employee>` — only supplied fields are updated; `id`, `createdAt` are never overwritten.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `EmploymentStatus` enum used in `Employee.employmentStatus` must be the exact same enum exported from `src/shared/types/index.ts` — no local redefinition, no string literal union.

The `Employee` entity field names and types must match the reconciled architecture in `.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json` — specifically the `domain_entities[].attributes` for the Employee entity: id (string), employeeNumber (string), firstName (string), lastName (string), email (string), managerId (string | null), department (string), hireDate (Date), terminationDate (Date | null), employmentStatus (EmploymentStatus), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date).
The `IEmployeeRepository` method signatures must match the interface declared in the reconciled architecture's module boundaries: the `employee` module owns the `EmployeeRepository interface`.

integrationPoints.why: The Employee entity imports `EmploymentStatus` enum. This is the only external dependency for this phase.
